sections.overview: The European Field Cricket is a ground-dwelling cricket of warm, open habitats across much of Europe.
sections.identification: It is a stout, glossy black cricket with a large rounded head and yellowish forewing bases; short hindwings leave it flightless. The UK species account adds that the hindwings are vestigial.
sections.habitat: It favours short, warm turf and bare patches on dry, often sandy or chalky ground, where it excavates a burrow.
sections.diet: It eats grasses and herbs, with small invertebrates and carrion also recorded in some regional accounts.
sections.behavior: Males sing from burrow entrances, producing a loud repeated chirp that attracts females.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in soil; the young hatch after several weeks and overwinter as nymphs before becoming adults the following season.
sections.ecology: The burrow provides refuge and nesting space; dependence on warm, short vegetation distinguishes it ecologically from woodland crickets such as Nemobius sylvestris.
sections.conservation: Regional conservation reports link declines to loss of suitable open grassland, although status varies by country and region.
